_comment: Multiple engage target cycling (#1084): UnitCombat.strike() only ever damages whichever ONE enemy target_enemy currently resolves to, so a MULTIPLE_ENGAGE unit genuinely fighting 2+ distinct adjacent enemy regiments at once used to keep every strike locked onto whichever one it engaged first -- the other sat in FIGHTING state taking zero casualties indefinitely. This scenario keeps one player Spearmen regiment (team 0, uid 0, 70 soldiers) stationary and centred while two smaller enemy Infantry regiments (team 1, uid 1 and uid 2, 18 soldiers each) auto-advance on it from different bearings -- one from due south, one from the south-west. At tick 8, before either enemy reaches contact, the player selects the unit and issues Ctrl+F2 (Multiple engage). Verified via dump-state.sh: uid 1 reaches contact first (~tick 170), uid 2 reaches contact by ~tick 260, and target_enemy then rotates between them -- both uid 1's and uid 2's soldier counts drop across the remainder of the clip instead of only the first one engaged. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd. World coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
